assumptions: Qualified partners perform field survey and repair work while the founder owns analysis, workflow, measurement design, and commercial coordination.
Customers provide sufficient meter and production data to normalize the baseline and accept a pre-agreed independent savings methodology.
The founder keeps initial delivery to two or three sites and does not leave employment before repeatable demand, contribution economics, and personal runway are demonstrated.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Three to five paid plant pilots showing pre-repair loss, implementation rate, verified twelve-month savings, attribution stability, gross contribution after field and channel costs, sales-cycle length, renewal or multi-site expansion, and a direct benchmark against incumbent audit offers.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Compressed-air leakage is a measurable operating loss, and combining a survey with repair verification and performance pricing aligns payment to savings. The insight is commercially sound but well known: compressor vendors and energy-service firms already market leak audits, so the opportunity rests on execution and positioning rather than a hidden mechanism.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Wasted electricity, lost compressor capacity, and avoidable maintenance are direct economic pains with identifiable plant budget owners, and the existence of commercial leak-audit services supports willingness to buy remediation. Plant-specific loss value, repair priority, and acceptance of a shared-savings contract remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A paid initial survey reduces cash risk and a share of verified savings creates meaningful upside and repeat revenue. Attractive owner earnings are plausible on large sites, but field labor, travel, metering, calibration, partner share, long enterprise sales, customer-controlled repairs, baseline disputes, and post-verification cash collection can materially compress contribution margin and payback.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish plants with substantial compressed-air loads and limited internal energy analytics are a focused, reachable beachhead with sufficiently valuable facilities to support B2B pricing. The packet does not quantify the number of qualifying plants, their compressor spend, leak backlog, or concentration by geography and channel.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor-neutral measurement and payment tied to independently verified savings can differentiate the service. Established compressor OEMs, maintenance firms, auditors, and ESCOs already possess site access, credibility, field teams, and the ability to bundle monitoring or repairs, making a dominant position difficult without a protected channel or proprietary operating edge.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful contract can expand from one line to an entire plant, recur through leak re-surveys, and extend to multiple sites or other measurable industrial utilities. The baseline, work-order, and verification workflow provides a credible adjacency path, although new equipment categories require additional expertise and measurement rules.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Longitudinal leak signatures, repair costs, and persistence outcomes could improve prioritization and benchmarking. Those data are initially customer-controlled, the proposed agreement is nonexclusive and replaceable, and neither durable data rights nor channel exclusivity currently prevents an incumbent or specialist from copying the workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Independent baselining, a tagged repair backlog, persistence checks, and performance-linked fees can be materially more decision-useful and lower-risk than an equipment-led spot audit. The advantage is not yet quantified against existing vendors on savings captured, audit price, implementation rate, trust, or time to payback.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The cited 2026 audit deadline creates a near-term management trigger, while energy cost and efficiency pressure make quantified savings relevant. Compliance audits need not produce leak-remediation purchases, and an imminent deadline may favor already-established accredited providers rather than a new entrant.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accredited auditors, compressor service firms, distributors, and factory associations are plausible concentrated channels, and relatively few high-value accounts may suit the founder better than mass-market selling. Channel partners already own the relationships and can bundle the offer, while direct industrial sales are slow, trust-heavy, and not yet demonstrated as repeatable or affordable.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Analytics, anomaly detection, reporting, and partner coordination fit the founder, and the proposed capital requirement is within the stated limit. Safe field access, calibrated measurement, credible verification, production-normalized baselines, customer repair execution, insurance, accreditation support, and partner management make delivery substantially more operational than a software business and challenging alongside full-time employment.

highest_value_structural_change: Partner exclusively with an accredited auditor or independent service network in one industrial cluster and package a fixed, production-normalized baseline plus repair-persistence guarantee that incumbent equipment-led audits do not offer.
main_structural_strength: The service targets a directly measurable energy loss and combines an upfront paid diagnostic with outcome-linked upside, creating a credible route to positive cash generation before software-scale expansion.
primary_score_limiter: Incumbent service providers already control plant relationships and field capability, while the proposed venture lacks a protected channel, exclusive data right, or proven advantage large enough to overcome that position.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established compressor vendors already sell leak-detection programs, demonstrating demand but undermining novelty and making it likely that audits, monitoring, and repairs can be bundled by suppliers with existing site trust.
